name: Bazedoxifene

lead: Bazedoxifene is a prescription SERM used for osteoporosis prevention and, with conjugated estrogens, for menopausal symptoms.
Published research concerns bone and menopause; no studies on appearance exist in the sources reviewed.

paras: It binds estrogen receptors and acts like estrogen in bone while blocking estrogen in tissues such as the uterus, per preclinical work.

The combination product carries a boxed warning for endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia. Common effects include muscle spasms, nausea and diarrhea. It is prescription-only and contraindicated in pregnancy.

lead: Bazedoxifene is a third-generation selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) of the 2-phenylindole class, taken by mouth. It is used for the prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis and, combined with conjugated estrogens as Duavee or Duavive, for menopausal vasomotor symptoms [1][2].

It is not a hair, skin or muscle treatment, and the sources reviewed contain no appearance-related studies. It is included here because SERMs as a class are discussed in hormone and physique communities.

A 3-year randomized trial in women with osteoporosis found fewer new vertebral fractures than placebo [3]. The combination product Duavee carries a boxed warning about endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia [2].
infobox: Conbriza, Viviant; with conjugated estrogens: Duavee, Duavive

paras: Bazedoxifene alone is used in some countries to prevent postmenopausal osteoporosis, offered as an alternative for women who cannot or prefer not to use bisphosphonates [1]. In the US it is available only in combination with conjugated estrogens, for moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis in women with a uterus [2].

In four placebo-controlled trials of the combination product, adverse reactions at 5% or more included muscle spasms, nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, upper abdominal pain, throat pain, dizziness and neck pain [2]. The label boxed warning covers endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia, and the product is contraindicated in pregnancy [2].

Bazedoxifene binds estrogen receptors and acts as an agonist or antagonist depending on the tissue [1]. Preclinical work reported that it bound estrogen receptor alpha, increased bone density and strength in rats and had limited effects on the uterus and breast cancer cell proliferation [4].

A 3-year randomized, placebo- and raloxifene-controlled trial in 6,847 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis found a significantly lower incidence of new vertebral fractures with bazedoxifene 20 or 40 mg than placebo [3]. Network meta-analyses of fracture-prevention drugs include bazedoxifene among SERMs [5]. Trials of bazedoxifene combined with conjugated estrogens examined menopausal symptoms and bone loss prevention [6][7]. Registered studies have also examined it in multiple sclerosis, schizophrenia, breast cancer and glucocorticoid-induced bone loss [8][9]. No study of bazedoxifene for appearance purposes was found.

The European Medicines Agency approved bazedoxifene on 27 April 2009, and the US FDA approved it in 2013 as part of Duavee; Pfizer is listed as developer [1]. Phase 3 osteoporosis trials began around 2001 [10].
Bazedoxifene is being studied for breast and pancreatic cancer, with a 2013 report describing growth inhibition of breast cancer cells including resistant tumors [1].

timeline.event: FDA approves Duavee (bazedoxifene with conjugated estrogens) [1].
